subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A psychologist shows a person a series of ambiguous inkblot images and asks them to describe what they see, analysing the responses to infer unconscious aspects of their personality. This projective personality assessment technique is called the:
explanation: The Rorschach Inkblot Test uses ambiguous inkblot images to elicit projections of unconscious thoughts and feelings, distinct from the TAT (which uses picture scenes).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch9 — Personality & Motivation (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A psychologist shows a person ambiguous pictures of people in various scenes and asks them to make up a story about what is happening, analysing the story's themes to infer the person's unconscious needs and conflicts. This projective personality assessment technique is called the:
explanation: The TAT uses ambiguous picture scenes and has the person construct a narrative, from which underlying motives and conflicts are inferred.
